messages.subject: GRM using a centered identity-by-state (IBS)
messages.body_plain:
Hi  Luis,

I want a script  to  construct a genomic relationship matrix (GRM) relationships among accessions using a centered identity-by-state (IBS) approach, following Endelman and Jannink (2012) and  visualizing using a heatmap, with hierarchical clustering performed using the unweighted pair group method with arithmetic mean (UPGMA) cluster algorithm.

Thanks

Nigus

messages.subject: Re: GRM using a centered identity-by-state (IBS)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nigus,

Here’s one way to do it in dartR:

library(dartRverse)

# Genomic relationship matrix
G <- gl.grm(platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>)

# Heatmap with UPGMA
gl.plot.heatmap(G,
                x = platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>,
                hclustfun = function(d) hclust(d, method = "average"))

Before running this, you’ll need to install the development version of dartR.base. To install it:

1. Clear your RStudio workspace (Session > Clear Workspace). This removes all objects in your environment, so make sure you can recreate them from your script.
2. Restart R (Session > Restart R).
3. Run the following:

install.packages(c("dartR.captive", "rrBLUP", "dendextend"))
devtools::install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR.base@dev")

When the installation finishes, check that you see: DONE (dartR.base) at the end of the output.

Google Groups sometimes changes quotation marks in R code, so please double-check them after pasting the code into RStudio.

Cheers,
Luis

messages.body_plain:
Hi Nigus,

Two alleles are Identical by State (IBS) if they are the same allele (for example, both are A). Two alleles are Identical by Descent (IBD) if they are inherited from a common ancestor. So IBD alleles are always IBS, but not all IBS alleles are IBD, because two copies of the same allele can come from different, unrelated ancestors. With SNP data, we can see whether two individuals have the same allele (IBS), but not whether those alleles were inherited from a common ancestor (IBD). For this reason, most methods measure IBS, including the Endelman and Jannink (2012) matrix, which gl.grm calculates. IBD can only be inferred, from a pedigree or with more complex methods.

The “figure margins too large” error comes from RStudio because your plot panel window was too small to display the heatmap. To solve it, increase the size of this panel with your mouse or use plotheatmap = FALSE as below.

To change the title of the plot, you can use the parameter main, as shown below.

G <- gl.grm(platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>, plotheatmap = FALSE)

gl.plot.heatmap(G,
                x = platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>,
                hclustfun = function(d) hclust(d, method = "average"),
                main = "Genomic relationship matrix (centred IBS)")

Cheers,
Luis
